newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler sees realistic hope for EMU target.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler sees realistic hope for EMU target.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Monday he thought Germany had a realistic chance of meeting the deficit criterion for European monetary union (EMU).

Zeitler said at a gathering of bankers in Munich it was too early to make firm predictions but if economic growth did not wreck the government's plans, Bonn had a realistic chance of making the deficit target even if it was interpreted strictly.
He said current specualtion about a postponement of EMU, due to start in 1999, was "premature."
Zietler, head of the central bank in the southern state of Bavaria, also said he thought the dollar's recent recovery was based on economic fundamentals but had now come to an end.
"The last phase of the dollar's recovery was a phase of normalisation, which has now come to an end," he said.
